title:
Space engineering
Communications
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Section (prepared by the ECSS-E-ST-50C Revision Working Group)
status_notes: Second issue, Revision 1, dated 1 March 2021. It revises ECSS-E-ST-50C of 31 July 2008, which followed ECSS-E-50 Part 1A (20 October 2003) and Part 2A (4 July 2005); ECSS-E-ST-50B was never issued (change log, p. 3). Changes from the 2008 issue are shown with revision tracking. Whether a later revision exists is not stated in the document.

contents.title: Terms specific to the present standard
Communication system architectural design document (CSADD) - DRD (normative)
Communication system detailed design document (CSDDD) - DRD (normative)

key_points.text: The standard covers space-ground and space-to-space links and the AIT links to the spacecraft; it details the space link and space network domains and covers the ground network only as needed for end-to-end services (other ground aspects are in ECSS-E-ST-70).

For control operations the objective is guaranteed, in-order delivery of commands (commands may be repeated, never lost); for payload data the goal is to move as much data as possible, accepting some loss.

Table in clause 4.2: ECSS-E-AS-50-21 (CCSDS 131.0-B-3) supersedes ECSS-E-ST-50-01C; -22 (132.0-B-2) the TM Transfer Frame of ECSS-E-ST-50-03C; -23 (732.0-B-3) adds AOS; -24 (231.0-B-3), -25 (232.0-B-3) and -26 (232.1-B-2) replace clauses 8-9, 5-6 and 7 of ECSS-E-ST-50-04C.

Figure 4-2 places CCSDS and Internet protocols on the OSI layers (CFDP, BP/LTP, IP over CCSDS, Space Packet and Encapsulation, TC/TM/AOS/USLP/Proximity-1 data links, coding sublayers, RF) and cites ECSS-E-ST-70-41C as an example of an application-specific source/sink.
The communication engineering milestones are SRR, PDR, CDR, QR, AR, ORR and FRR, following the ECSS-E-ST-10 process.

A service guaranteeing in-sequence delivery of telecommands is required (5.4.2), and the probability of accepting an erroneous telecommand must be below 10^-2/N, N being the number of TCs expected over the mission (5.4.3).

Essential telecommands must be decodable and distributed even when all other systems, including the CDMU, are non-operational; for critical operations they must not depend on software, and their list is agreed at PDR.
TC encryption is required when authentication alone cannot meet the security requirements; SDLS in ECSS-E-AS-50-25 is cited as a data-link option.

New in Rev.1: hot-redundant TC chains must avoid repeatedly selecting the channel with lower signal quality (dual-lock issue, see ECSS-E-HB-50 clause 4.4.5.2), and all telecommands must carry a destination spacecraft identifier.
All telemetry must carry a source spacecraft identifier and be time-stamped against a common on-board reference time; telemetry-in-the-blind must be supported.
Uplink budgets assume a BER of 10^-5 at the TC decoder input; at that BER the uplink frame rejection rate for 256-octet frames must be below 10^-5.

With BCH coding, the probability of undetected uplink frame error can be below 10^-18 with frame error control and below 10^-8 without; downlink frame rejection should be below 10^-5 and acceptance of corrupted maximum-size frames below 10^-12.
An application for frequency assignment must be made to the ITU Radiocommunication Bureau before SRR.
Space link frames must identify the spacecraft and link; data units must carry a source/destination identifier and a sequence identifier, and the protocol must include error detection.

The space link must provide guaranteed and expedited delivery, time correlation of on-board time with ground time, ranging and/or Doppler tracking, TC receipt confirmation at the space network gateway, and exception reporting.

Eight DRDs are defined (CSRD, CSBD, CSAD, CSVP, CSADD, CSDDD, CSPD, CSOM). The CSPD records frequency, protocol, address, channel and SCID assignments and is the formal statement of compliance to ECSS-E-50.

notes: Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers, and PDF page 90 is blank (the registry gives 89 pages). Figure 4-2 is a diagram whose labels are extracted as jumbled text (p. 21). The 'mentioned' entries above come from the figure and running text, not from a reference list. The change log lists two 'Annex F' updates, the second carrying the CSPD title, which is actually Annex G (p. 3). Clause 4.3.2 is still headed 'Space network' although the change log says the term was replaced by 'on-board network' (p. 22). The bibliography cites the 2021 adoption notices with their 2021 CCSDS base issues (131.0-B-3, 132.0-B-2, 732.0-B-3, 231.0-B-3, 232.0-B-3, 232.1-B-2), not the later Rev.1 notices. Annex I opens with a stray 'A-A-' artefact (p. 86). The Figure 4-2 note contains the typo 'axample' (p. 21).
